raw_response:
I farm 600 mu, so I can't manage it like a tiny household plot. I have to think about yield, cost, and whether three people in the family can keep up, so I use machinery where I can and hire labor for the busy periods. Since I have well irrigation, I am not farming blind, but pumping water costs money, so I do not want to chase the very highest yield on every mu. I would rather keep a steady plan that has worked around here: a big block in wheat-maize rotation for stable grain income, then cotton and stevia on separate land for cash. With my experience, I trust what I have seen in my own fields and what other capable farmers nearby are doing. I am not going to change too much this year. I will keep about 300 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, 180 mu in cotton, and 120 mu in stevia. On wheat and maize I will stay a bit above the minimum fertilizer rate, because if grain goes yellow from underfeeding, the loss is bigger than the extra fertilizer bill. On cotton and stevia I will watch spending more carefully, because those crops need more labor and more management.

For wheat, as of April 18, 2026, the crop is already in the ground from last autumn, so my main decision now is water and topdressing, then harvest in early June. After wheat harvest, I need to move fast into maize, because the turnaround is tight and I do not have time for slow field work on 300 mu. Cotton I will keep on land that is easier to manage and irrigate, and I will split fertilizer a few times because that crop responds better that way. Stevia can make money, but it is not as easy as wheat-maize, so I keep it at 120 mu, not more. I need hired labor for cotton picking and for some stevia work, otherwise the family cannot finish on time.
